notes: Extracted unchanged except: anonymous rules named rule:quant-*; the example's dprod:dutyState triples removed (evaluator output); odrl:conflict odrl:prohibit made explicit; ODRL includedIn edges added. dprod:acceptsOffer, dprod:effectiveDate and dprod:expirationDate are metadata, never evaluated. Obligations in due2. The three duties are root obligations with no constraints, so no guards: each is in force for exactly the requests some rule of the contract matches, constraints aside (due2-workflows.md §5.2) — scenarios 1 and 2 — and for no other (scenarios 3–5: a request on another target, or by the provider, matches no rule). Bearers: interiorisation gives every duty the policy-level odrl:assignee quant-research, but for each role a value the rule states beats an interiorised one (due2-workflows.md §4), so dprod:subjectOfDuty decides: data-platform-team bears delivery and notify, quant-research bears report. This resolves the 'two bearers' finding of the previous version. History. Because the three are in force for the same requests and have no guards, a due2 case history activates them in the same trace (due2-profiles.md §7: instances are activated separately, but here they are first owed together); the SOTW of scenarios 1 and 2 uses the example's one explicit activation, report-2026-001 at 2026-02-01T00:00Z, for all three. These entries are not the default: without them each would be activated at effective_at, and the delivery duty would have no occurrence yet. notify-2026-001's 'Pending' in the example has no due2 counterpart (an obligation in force is owed). The RRULE has no DTSTART, so it is anchored at the duty's activation; the anchor 2026-02-01T00:00 is not generated by the rule and so is not an occurrence (§7), and the occurrences are 06:00 daily from 2026-02-01. Recurring instances are reported one per occurrence, with an extra 'instance' field (the occurrence time) that the case format does not define. With only the example's one delivery (2026-02-09T06:12Z) in evidence, the 02-09 instance is fulfilled; every other instance, 02-01 to 02-08 and 02-10, has no witness with t ≤ occurred_at ≤ t + PT30M and is violated. The 02-09 and 02-10 statuses match the example's annotations. DPROD's own performed() has no time lower bound (§5.4), so its rules would fulfil the 02-10 instance with the 02-09 delivery; the annotation follows the intent, not DPROD's text (due2-profiles.md §7). Exception 2 (DPROD-only state): the example's Σ is not the one DPROD's rules would derive from this evidence, so the two evaluators are compared on decisions, which agree, not on duty states. The violated delivery instances of scenario 1 are reported and do not affect the verdict (due2-workflows.md §6.1); DPROD permits too, because it never collects the delivery duty for a display request (due2-profiles.md §8.2, exception 6). DPROD Σ assumed, matching the example's dutyState annotations as of 2026-02-10T09:00Z: delivery-2026-001 has a 2026-02-10T06:00 instance that is Violated and a Fulfilled 2026-02-09 instance; notify-2026-001 is Pending; report-2026-001 is Active with activatedAt 2026-02-01; performed = {(data-platform-team, deliver, market-prices, 2026-02-09T06:12Z)}. In DPROD the duties are collected only when their action matches the request (step 1), and a collected violation denies only after a permission matched (step 6 follows step 5); no permission shares an action with a duty, so Σ, deadlines and recurrence change no DPROD decision and all five scenarios agree with due2 under ignore (the 'duty collection' gap of §8.2). DPROD can never collect notify-2026-001 or report-2026-001: a request on their targets fails the policy-target gate (§7.3), and a request on market-prices fails their asset match, so the example's 'Active' state for report-2026-001 cannot be reached by §7.2 (scenario 4).

scenarios.name: consumer displays while the provider is in breach of today's delivery

expected.why: rule:quant-display applies and is ready: Permit. It matches, so all three obligations are in force. Delivery instances run daily at 06:00 from activation, each due 30 minutes later: 02-01 to 02-08 have no witness by their deadlines and are violated; the 02-09 delivery at 06:12 witnesses the 02-09 instance only: a witness for an instance must have occurred_at ≥ t (due2-profiles.md §7), so the 02-10 instance has none and is violated at 06:30. notify is due 02-15 and report 03-03, both outstanding. None affects the verdict (§6.1).

scenarios.dprod_expected: Permit (grantorDuties = granteeDuties = violations = ∅: no duty matches display, so the Violated delivery instance is never collected)

scenarios.name: consumer redistributes

expected.why: rule:quant-no-distribute applies; no permission covers distribute. Deny. The prohibition matches, so the obligations are in force, with the statuses of scenario 1 (same history, same instant).

scenarios.dprod_expected: Deny (step 4; under the literal §7.4 direction step 1 also collects delivery-2026-001, since deliver includedIn distribute, but step 4 returns first)

scenarios.name: provider asks to display under the consumer's rights

expected.why: Every permission names quant-research as assignee, so the party part is F for data-platform-team; the prohibition is on distribute. NotApplicable. No rule matches, so no obligation is in force.

scenarios.dprod_expected: NotApplicable (the policy is applicable because the agent is the grantor, but each rule has its own subject; contrast dprod-divergences scenario 1)

scenarios.name: consumer files its usage report

expected.why: Every rule takes the policy target market-prices, and usage-stats is not part of it, so no rule matches: NotApplicable. An obligation is in force only through its policy's rules, never through its own action, so performing report-2026-001 does not put it in force; its status for this request is not reported (request-independent monitoring is open, due2-workflows.md §9 #4).

scenarios.dprod_expected: NotApplicable (step 0: usage-stats does not match the policy target market-prices, so report-2026-001 is never collected or updated)

scenarios.name: provider performs its delivery

expected.why: No permission covers deliver. rule:quant-no-distribute matches the action (deliver ⊑ distribute) and the target, but its assignee is quant-research, so it does not match the provider. No rule matches, so delivery-2026-001 is not in force for this request, although its bearer (dprod:subjectOfDuty) is the requester. NotApplicable.

scenarios.dprod_expected: NotApplicable (step 1 collects delivery-2026-001 into grantorDuties and step 3 activates the 2026-02-11 instance, but step 5 returns NotApplicable before duties are reported)
